{{nihongo|'''Jogu Shrine'''|常宮神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echizen Province]].

=== Company name ===
Tsunenomiya Shrine was also called ``Tsunenomiya'', ``Tsunenomiya Gozen'', and ``Tsunenomiya Daigongen'' in ancient times. The name ``Jonomiya'' is said to be named after {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}'s {{ill|Oracle|Q217123|qid=Q217123}}, ``Always enjoy the palace, where the waves and wind are calm.''{{Sfn|Jonomiya Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981|p=523-524}}. In ancient times, it was read as ``tsune (no) miya,'' but in the early modern period, it was read as ``jougu,'' and in the first year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} ( The current name and pronunciation of the company was set in {{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}}).

Also, ``{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Q1052905|qid=Q1052905}}'' and ``{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' from the middle of the {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292}} {{ill|Q1106 4932|qid=Q1106 4932|lt=Tenyaoyorozuhime Shrine (Ame no Yorozu Himejinja), which can be seen in the Shinmeicho}}, is said to be the name of the ancient Tokomiya Shrine {{Sfn|Tokomiya Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981|p=523-524}} (there are also different theories<ref group="note" name="Tenyaoyorozu Himakami"/>).In addition, Tsunemiya Shrine had a deep relationship with {{ill|Kehi Shrine|Q11129346|qid=Q11129346}}, so in ancient times it was also referred to as ``Hongu/Setsusha'', ``Kuchinomiya/Okumiya'', ``Himoroginomiya/Kagami no Miya'', ``Kamisha/Shimosha'', etc.{{Sfn|Kehi Shrine (Gods)|1985|p=125-127}}.

=== Enshrined God ===
The following seven deities are enshrined in the Shrine History Book. </ref>.
; Main shrine (main shrine)
:* ``Amenoyorozuhime no Mikoto'' (Amenoya Oyorozuhime no Mikoto) - Commonly known as ``Tokomiya Okami''.
:* {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} (Jingu Kougou) - Empress of Emperor Chuai.
:* {{ill|Emperor Chūai|ar|الإمبراطور تشواي|arz|الامبراطور تشواى|azb|چوای (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Chūai|cs|Čúai|de|Chūai|es|Chūai Tennō|fa|امپراتور چوآی|fr|Chūai|hr|Chūai|hu|Csúai japán császár|id|Kaisar Chūai|it|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|ka|ტიუაი|ko|주아이 천황|nl|Chuai|pl|Chūai|pt|Chuai|ru|Император Тюай|sh|Car Chūai|simple|Emperor Chūai|sl|Cesar Čuaj|sv|Chuai|th|จักรพรรดิชูไอ|tl|Emperador Chūai|tr|Chūai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тюай|uz|Imperator Chūai|vi|Thiên hoàng Chūai|zh|仲哀天皇|zh_min_nan|Tyûai Thian-hông|zh_yue|仲哀天皇|qid=Q179971}} - 14th Emperor.
; 4 shrines surrounding the main shrine
:* East Palace: {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Nihon Takeru}} (Yamato Takeru Mikoto)
:* Sojagu Shrine: {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}} (Oujin Tennou) - 15th Emperor.
:* Tairadenomiya: Tamahime no Mikoto (Tamahime no Mikoto, Tamahime no Mikoto) - Empress Jingu's younger sister.
:* West Palace: {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668|lt=Takeuchi Sukune no Mikoto}} (Takeuchi Sukune no Mikoto)According to the shrine's legend, Ten Yaoyoroman Hime no Mikoto has been enshrined since ancient times as the god of sericulture, so it is thought that Ten Yaomo Hime no Mikoto is a local deity. The other six pillars are based on the legend of Empress Jingu going to war. (Japan)|Q1346269|Taiho}}3 ({{ill|703|Q23500|qid=Q23500}}), it is said to have been jointly enshrined in {{Sfn|Kehi Shrine (Gods)|1985|p =125-127}}, and it is speculated that this was a combined enshrinement as the Hachiman faith spread at the time. These enshrined deities are the same as {{ill|Kehi Shrine|Q11129346|qid=Q11129346}}, except that the main deity enshrined is Ten Yaoyoroman Hime no Mikoto (the main deity enshrined at Kehi Shrine) rather than Izabetsu no Mikoto (the main deity enshrined at Kehi Shrine). Tsunegu-jingu is said to have a close relationship with Kehi-jingu, and one theory is that the Sosansai (regular festival), which is attended by pilgrims from Kehi-jingu Shrine, is a Shinto ritual in which Izabetsu-no-Mikoto visits Tenyaomanhi-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Kehi-jingu Shrine (Gods)|1985|p=125-127}}.As for the deities enshrined in the main shrine, it is stated in the ``Jōmiya Honki'' and the detailed account book of {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}}3 ({{ill|1718|Q6899|qid=Q6899}}) that there are three deities as mentioned above. However, according to another theory, in "Kehigu Shrine" (an old record of {{ill|Kehi Shrine|Q11129346|qid=Q11129346}}), there are two deities enshrined, and the main deity is Empress Jingu, and "Ten Yaoyoromanhi Mikoto" is said to be the same. It is said to be another name for Emperor Chuai, and it is said that Emperor Chuai is enshrined in the {{ill|Aidono|Q135009883|qid=Q135009883}}.

It is said that Empress Jingu gave birth to {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}} in Tsukushi while wearing a belly band at Jogu Shrine, so Tsunegu Shrine is worshiped as the deity of safe childbirth. It is also said that Empress Jingu prayed for safe passage on sea routes during the {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}}, so she is also worshiped as the guardian deity of navigation and fishing.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
[[File:Kehi-jingu otorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|{{ill|Kehi Shrine|Q11129346|qid=Q11129346}} ({{ill|Tsuruga, Fukui|ar|تسوروغا (فوكوي)|azb|تسوروقا، فوکوئی|ce|Цуруга|ceb|Tsuruga-shi|cs|Curuga (Fukui)|de|Tsuruga|es|Tsuruga|eu|Tsuruga (Fukui)|fa|تسوروگا، فوکوئی|fi|Tsuruga|fr|Tsuruga|gl|Tsuruga|id|Tsuruga, Fukui|it|Tsuruga|ja|敦賀市|ko|쓰루가시|lt|Curuga|mg|Tsuruga|ms|Tsuruga|mzn|تسوروگا، فوکوئی|nl|Tsuruga|pl|Tsuruga|pt|Tsuruga|ro|Tsuruga|ru|Цуруга|simple|Tsuruga, Fukui|sv|Tsuruga|tg|Тсуруга|th|สึรูงะ|tl|Tsuruga, Fukui|tr|Tsuruga|tt|Цуруга|uk|Цуруґа|ur|ٹسوروگا، فوکوئی|uz|Tsuruga|vi|Tsuruga, Fukui|war|Tsuruga, Fukui|zh|敦賀市|zh_classical|敦賀市|zh_min_nan|Turuga-chhī|zh_yue|敦賀|qid=Q847581}}Akebono Town)}}{{small|{{ill|Echizen Province|ceb|Echizen|cs|Provincie Ečizen|de|Provinz Echizen|es|Provincia de Echizen|fa|ولایت اچیزن|fr|Province d'Echizen|gl|Provincia de Echizen|id|Provinsi Echizen|it|Echizen (provincia)|ja|越前国|ko|에치젠국|lt|Ečidzeno žemė|nl|Echizen (provincie)|pt|Província de Echizen|ru|Этидзэн (провинция)|simple|Echizen Province|sk|Ečizen (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечизен|tr|Echizen (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Етідзен|zh|越前國|zh_min_nan|Etizen-kok|zh_yue|越前國|qid=Q1047144}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}. It has a deep relationship with Tsunemiya Shrine. }}]]
According to the shrine's legend, the main enshrined deity, Ten Yaoyoromanhiba-no-Mikoto, has resided here since ancient times. After {{ill|Emperor Chūai|ar|الإمبراطور تشواي|arz|الامبراطور تشواى|azb|چوای (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Chūai|cs|Čúai|de|Chūai|es|Chūai Tennō|fa|امپراتور چوآی|fr|Chūai|hr|Chūai|hu|Csúai japán császár|id|Kaisar Chūai|it|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|ka|ტიუაი|ko|주아이 천황|nl|Chuai|pl|Chūai|pt|Chuai|ru|Император Тюай|sh|Car Chūai|simple|Emperor Chūai|sl|Cesar Čuaj|sv|Chuai|th|จักรพรรดิชูไอ|tl|Emperador Chūai|tr|Chūai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тюай|uz|Imperator Chūai|vi|Thiên hoàng Chūai|zh|仲哀天皇|zh_min_nan|Tyûai Thian-hông|zh_yue|仲哀天皇|qid=Q179971}}, the Emperor and {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} worshiped Kehijin in February 2010. When going on a conquest|Q11249435}}, the Emperor went alone to Nagato via Kii, but the Empress remained at the permanent palace, plotting a foreign expedition, and reported that she set out on the first day of the rabbit in June.<ref name="historical book"/>. Then {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} 3rd year ({{ill|703|Q23500|qid=Q23500}}), the shrine building was repaired by imperial order, and {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} and {{jalink|Emperor Chuai|Q179971} }, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Nippon Takeru no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}, Tamahime no Mikoto, {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668|lt=Takeuchi Sukune no Mikoto}} are reported to have been enshrined together.<ref name="historical book"/>. After that, it was said to have operated as a shrine outside the precincts of Kehi Shrine.On the other hand, according to "Kehigushaki", during the reign of Emperor Kanmu, the divine spirit of Empress Jingu appeared and gave an oracle that said, "I will always stay in the palace," so the Empress was praised and enshrined as "Ten Yaoyoromanhiba Okami," and further, {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jowa}} There is a separate biography that states that he {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=solicited}} Empress Jingu in 11 years ({{ill|844|Q23835|qid=Q23835}}).

Behind the shrine grounds are a group of side caves that are thought to be from the late {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}} period, and because this area is an anchorage in Tsuruga Bay, it is thought that people settled there from an early time {{Sfn|Kehi Shrine (Gods)|1985|p=125-127}}. In connection with this, there is a theory that the beginning of the connection between Kehi Shrine and Tsunemiya Shrine lies in the relationship between the peacetime port (Tsurugazu) and the evacuation anchorage port (Jonomiya Bay) {{Sfn|Kehi Shrine (Gods)|1985|p=125-127}}.

=== Outline ===According to the national history, in {{ill|Saikō|Q1324664|qid=Q1324664}} 3rd year ({{ill|856|Q30370|qid=Q30370}}), ``Tenyaoyorozu Himejin'' was listed as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=government shrine}}. In the same year, the same god was enshrined as {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} {{Sfn|Jonomiya Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981|p=523-524}}. Also {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}} ink|Echizen Province|Q1047144}}{{ill|Tsuruga District, Fukui|ja|敦賀郡|ko|쓰루가군|zh|敦賀郡|qid=Q11499560}} {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi Shrine}} can be found listed as ``Tenyaoyorozu Hime Shrine''{{Sfn|Jonomiya Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981|p=523-524}}. Later, in the ``Echizen Domestic Shinto Name Book,'' there is a mention of ``Junior Second Rank Ten Yaoyorozu Hiba Daimyojin.'' Tsunemiya Shrine is thought to correspond to the "Tenyaoyorozu Hime-kami" seen in these documents {{Sfn|Tsunemiya Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981|p=523-524}} (However, there are different theories<ref group="Note" name="Tenyaoyorozu Himejin">In addition to Tsunemiya Shrine, Tenyaoyorozu Himejin Shrine, the subsidiary shrine of {{ill|Ōshio Hachimangu|Q11434131|qid=Q11434131}} in {{ill|Echizen, Fukui|Q877941|qid=Q877941}}, is mentioned in the essay about "Tenyaoyorozu Himejin", but no conclusion has been reached. {{Harv|Ten Yaoyoroman Hime Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986|p=232-233}}).According to the shrine's legend, it was later rebuilt in 4 years ({{ill|1015|Q19245|qid=Q19245}}) by the priest Enshu of the {{ill|Tiantai|Q668188|qid=Q668188|lt=Tendai monk}}. According to later records, in {{ill|Kyōroku|Q1193418|qid=Q1193418}} 2nd year ({{ill|1529|Q6421|qid=Q6421}}), {{ill|Asakura Takakage|Q11068401|qid=Q11068401|lt=Takakage Asakura}} and {{ill|Asakura Kagetoshi|Q11068680|qid=Q11068680|lt=Kagenori}} repaired and built the east hall {{Sfn|Jonomiya Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981|p=523-524}}. Then, after the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} 2nd year ({{ill|1574|Q6680|qid=Q6680}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Bunroku}}4 ({{ill|1595|Q6782|qid=Q6782}}), {{ill|Tsuruga Castle|Q11255713|qid=Q11255713|lt=Tsuruga Castle Lord}} {{jalink|Otani} Yoshitsugu|Q386265}} established a temporary shrine, and in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}}7 ({{ill|1602|Q6727|qid=Q6727}}) Echizen Province The main shrine (main shrine) was built by the lord {{ill|Yūki Hideyasu|Q1130929|qid=Q1130929}}{{Sfn|Jonomiya Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981|p=523-524}}. === God level ===
A record of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} dedication to ``Tenyaoyorozu Himegami'' (there are different opinions about the dedication <ref group="note" name="Atenyaoyorozu Himegami"/>).
* Six Kingdoms Historical Period
** On September 17, {{ill|Saikō|Q1324664|qid=Q1324664}} 3rd year ({{ill|856|Q30370|qid=Q30370}}), it was listed as a government shrine (``{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Q1052905|qid=Q1052905}}'') - It is written as ``Tenyaoyorozu Himakami.''
** September 28, 856, Junior Fourth Rank (Junior Montoku Emperor Jitsuroku) - Written as ``Tenyaoyorozu Himajin.''
* After Six Kingdoms History
** Junior Second Rank (``Echizen Domestic Shinto Name Book'') - Written as ``Tenyaoyorozu Hima Daimyojin.''

=== Shinto priest ===
There is no {{ill|Shake (social class)|Q11588367|qid=Q11588367}} at Tsunemiya Shrine, and until {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}} in the Meiji era, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine priests}} of the Tendai sect performed rituals {{Sfn|Tenyaoyoromanhiba Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1986|p=237}}. As for the temples of shrine priests, there are six temples that can be seen in the {{ill|Munafuda|Q8008834|qid=Q8008834}} dated 1595: ``Hozobo'', ``Kojobo'', ``Jiyobo'', ``Jorizobo'', ``Izumizobo'', and ``Daijyobo'' {{Sfn|Ten Yaoyoromanhi Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1986|p=237}}. The above-mentioned shrine priests returned to secular life and became Shinto priests in April of the first year of the Meiji era ({{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}}), but the only one left now is the Miyamoto family, which descends from the Hozobo family.

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Jogu-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Main shrine/place of worship<br />(both tangible cultural properties designated by Fukui prefecture)}}]]
The precincts are 4,455 tsubo {{Sfn|Tsunemiya Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981|p=523-524}} (approximately 1.5 hectares). The main shrine building is a reconstruction from the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}. The main shrine was rebuilt in 1713|Q6873}} in the middle of the Edo period. Sangen-sha {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} has three rooms on the front (girder row) and three rooms on the side (between the beams), with one room between the beams in the front serving as the vestibule, and a one-room prayer hall attached to the front. The roof used to be {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}}, but now it has a copper plate roof. The main body is a circular pillar, and the front chamber and facing prayer are square pillars. The front chamber is one step lower than the main chamber, and there are carvings on the rainbow beams and other areas. It has been pointed out that the decoration and form of this main hall are similar to the old main hall of Kehi Jingu Shrine (built in the early Edo period, but burnt down in an air raid), and it is also thought that it is a form in which the rear part of the shrine's Ryoryu-zukuri style was omitted. This main shrine is designated as a tangible cultural property of Fukui Prefecture. <ref name="Explanation board">Precinct information board. </ref><ref name="Main shrine, place of worship, middle gate"/>The ``Place of Worship'' is a building with one room in the front and two sides on all sides (no walls or fittings), with a roof made of Karahafu style and copper plate. It was originally the middle gate (Mukakaramon) of Kehi Shrine, and was moved to its current location in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}18 ({{ill|1943|Q18623|qid=Q18623}}). {{harv|"Fukui Prefecture Shrine Journal"}} was written in {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}}14 ({{ill|1637|Q6889|qid=Q6889}}), the first {{ill|Obama Domain|Q1088442|qid=Q1088442|lt=Obama feudal lord}}, {{ill|Sakai Tadakatsu|Q7402768|qid=Q7402768|lt=Tadakatsu Sakai}}, but the detailed style suggests that it was built in the late Edo period. '''Chumon'''' was built in {{ill|Hōreki|Q1194397|qid=Q1194397}}12 ({{ill|1762|Q7652|qid=Q7652}}) in the middle of the Edo period. It is a four-legged gate with one room in the front and two rooms on the side, and the roof is made of copper plates. These places of worship and the middle gate, along with the main shrine, have been designated as tangible cultural properties of Fukui Prefecture. <ref name="Explanation board"/><ref name="Main shrine, place of worship, central gate"/>{{sfn|Tami. Yoshida (2009)|p=386-387}}Around the main shrine, there are four shrines, ``Higashidengu'''' (front east), ``Western shrine'' (front west), ``Soshagu'', and ``Tairadengu'' (both back east), similar to Kehi Jingu. Together with the main shrine, these shrines are called ``Daigoza'' {{Sfn|Ten Yaoyoromanhiba Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986|p=234}}. Other shrine buildings include a worship hall facing the sea where Kehi Shrine is worshiped, and a treasure trove that houses the Korean Bell, a national treasure.

In addition, there is a large tree called ``Ryutomatsu'' that stands along the sea's edge. It is said that a group of flames ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=ryutō}}) rise from the sea of ​​{{ill|Tsuruga Bay|Q11499550|qid=Q11499550}} and stay on this pine tree at dawn in the early hours of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=New Year's Day}}, and these lights are said to be offered to light the New Year's Day.{{Sfn|Jonomiya Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981|p=523-524}}.

There is a theory that the enshrined deity is {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|Q65318|qid=Q65318}}'s younger brother, {{ill|Wakatakehiko|Q11596350|qid=Q11596350|lt=Wakatake no Mikoto}}, but the details are unknown.

:* Shrine rank: Shikinaisha "Tenzu Shrine", Echizen Domestic Shinto Name Book "Sho Fourth Rank Tensujin" {{Sfn|Tenzu Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1986|p=255}}

: The enshrined deity is either {{ill|Kōra taisha|Q715647|qid=Q715647|lt=Kora Tadamari-myo}} or Tamasara Yoshihiko Shrine {{Sfn|Tamasa Yoshihiko Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986|p=257}}.

According to the "Nihon Montoku Emperor Annals," the four deities of Tenmokutsuhime, Tengokutsuhiko, Tensuzu, and Tamasara Yoshihiko, together with Tenyaoyorozuhime, are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Narihira}}3 ({{ill|856|Q30370|qid=Q30370}}), he was entrusted to a government shrine and was given the rank of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}, which is the lower rank of Junior Fifth Rank.

=== Festival ===
{{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469}} is held on {{ill|July 22|Q2725|qid=Q2725}} and is called ``''Sosansai'' (Sosansai/Sou no Umairi). This is a festival in which the gods of Kehi Shrine, along with the chief priest and other priests, visit Tokomiya Shrine, and it is a ritual that symbolizes the long-standing connection between Kehi Shrine and Tokomiya Shrine. During the festival, the divine spirits of the shrine are transported in a boat-shaped mikoshi, depart from Miyukihama on the barge ``Jingumaru'', and after a festival is held on the boat, they arrive at Tsunegu Shrine. Fishing is prohibited on this day, and fishermen tow the boats in small boats, believing that if they serve the barges, they will be blessed with a bountiful catch. As for its origin, there are two theories: one is based on a legend in which Empress Jingu led a military army to war, and the other is that the positive deity Kehi no Mikoto (Izabetsu no Mikoto) visits the negative deity Tsunegu no Mikoto (Ten Yaoyoromanhi no Mikoto). <ref name="Historic Book"/>{{Sfn|Kehi Shrine (Gods)|1985|p=125-127}}

In addition, until the early Meiji period, Shinto rituals based on the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hachiman faith}}, such as {{ill|Life release|Q11078912|qid=Q11078912}}, were held {{Sfn|Ten Yaoyoroman Hima Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986|p=237}}.

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
[[File:Jogu Jinsha Bell (261).jpg|thumb|150px|{{center|Joseon Bell (National Treasure)}}]]
* {{ill|Korean bell|Q11517870|qid=Q11517870}} (Craft)*: It is a large {{ill|Bonshō|Q8192099|qid=Q8192099}} with a total height of 112.0 cm and a diameter of 66.7 cm, and a celestial maiden statue is cast on the body. It is a Korean bell with a different style from the Japanese bell, and was made during the {{ill|Silla|Q28456|qid=Q28456|lt=Unified Silla}} period. There are inscriptions such as ``March date of the 7th year of Taiwa, Zhongcheng, Lianchi Temple, Jingzhou,'' but ``{{ill|Dahe Era|Q10934252|qid=Q10934252|lt=Taewa}}7'' is the year name of the Tang Dynasty and corresponds to {{ill|833|Q30377|qid=Q30377|lt=833 AD}}, and this bell is one of the few relics of Silla bells cast during the Unified Silla period. In the shrine biography, it is said that it was brought back from Korea during the {{ill|Imjin War|Q576338|qid=Q576338|lt=Bunroku no Eki}}, and in the second year of {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} ({{ill|1597|Q6790|qid=Q6790}}, {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}} dedicated {{ill|Ōtani Yoshitsugu|Q386265|qid=Q386265}} as a messenger to Tokomiya Shrine in honor of Empress Jingu's conquest of the Three Koreas. However, there is also a theory that it was brought by {{ill|Wokou|Q697605|qid=Q697605}}. It was designated as a national treasure on April 7, 1908, based on the then {{ill|Ancient Temples and Shrines Preservation Law|Q11411552|qid=Q11411552}}, and on November 22, 1952, it was designated as a national treasure based on {{ill|Cultural Properties Protection Law|Q1188502|qid=Q1188502}}. <ref>"Weekly Asahi Encyclopedia Japan's 84 National Treasures" (Asahi Shimbun, 1999), p.9-114 (commentary written by Eiichi Nomura). </ref><ref>{{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|201|366| Korean Bell}}<br />[http://info.pref.fukui.jp/bunka/bunkazai/sitei/kougei/jogujinja-chosensho.html Korean Bell] (Fukui Prefecture homepage). </ref><ref name="Explanation board"/>

'''Access'''
* From {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|Q502125|qid=Q502125}} (JR West) {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|Q1318747|qid=Q1318747}}, {{ill|Obama Line|Q1058227|qid=Q1058227}} {{ill|Tsuruga Station|Q5364670|qid=Q5364670}}
** Take the Fukutetsu Bus (Jonomiya Line bound for Tateishi) and get off at the "Jonomiya" bus stop (about 22 minutes, a short walk after getting off)

'''Surroundings'''
* Parrot stone
*: A huge rock 30 meters high and 21 meters wide located halfway up {{ill|Mount Saihō|Q11628327|qid=Q11628327}} (Saihogatake) behind the shrine. It is said that when you call out to this stone, human voices and bird calls are often heard in return, so it was named ``parrot stone''. It is also called the "word stone". Since it was discovered during the {{ill|Tenmei|de|Tenmei (Ära)|fa|تنمی|fr|Ère Tenmei|it|Tenmei|ja|天明|ko|덴메이|pt|Tenmei|ru|Тэммэй|simple|Tenmei|sr|Тенмеи|sv|Tenmei|th|เท็มเม|tr|Tenmei|zh|天明 (日本)|qid=Q1194121}} years ({{ill|1781|Q7719|qid=Q7719}}-{{ill|1789|ab|1789|af|1789|als|1789|am|1789 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1789|ar|1789|ary|1789|arz|1789|ast|1789|avk|1789|az|1789|azb|۱۷۸۹ (میلادی)|ba|1789 йыл|ban|1789|bcl|1789|be|1789|be_x_old|1789|bg|1789|bn|১৭৮৯|bo|༡༧༨༩ལོ།|bpy|মারি ১৭৮৯|br|1789|bs|1789.|ca|1789|cdo|1789 nièng|ce|1789 шо|ceb|1789|ckb|١٧٨٩|co|1789|crh|1789|cs|1789|csb|1789|cv|1789|cy|1789|da|1789|de|1789|diq|1789|el|1789|eml|1789|eo|1789|es|1789|et|1789|eu|1789|fa|۱۷۸۹ (میلادی)|fi|1789|fo|1789|fr|1789|frp|1789|frr|1789|fur|1789|fy|1789|ga|1789|gan|1789年|gcr|1789|gd|1789|gl|1789|gn|1789|gv|1789|he|1789|hi|१७८९|hif|1789|hr|1789.|hsb|1789|ht|1789 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1789|hy|1789|hyw|1789 թուական|ia|1789|id|1789|ilo|1789|inh|1789 шу|io|1789|is|1789|it|1789|ja|1789年|jv|1789|ka|1789|kaa|1789|kk|1789 жыл|kn|೧೭೮೯|ko|1789년|krc|1789 джыл|ku|1789|kv|1789-ӧд во|la|1789|lb|1789|lez|1789 йис|li|1789|lij|1789|lmo|1789|lt|1789 m.|lv|1789. gads|mai|१७८९|map_bms|1789|mdf|1789|mg|1789|mhr|1789|mi|1789|min|1789|mk|1789|mr|इ.स. १७८९|mrj|1789 и|ms|1789|my|၁၇၈၉|myv|1789 ие|mzn|۱۷۸۹|nah|1789|nap|1789|nds|1789|new|सन् १७८९|nl|1789|nn|1789|no|1789|nrm|1789|nso|1789|oc|1789|olo|1789|or|୧୭୮୯|os|1789-æм аз|pa|1789|pl|1789|pnb|1789|pt|1789|qu|1789|ro|1789|ru|1789 год|rue|1789|sa|१७८९|sah|1789|sc|1789|scn|1789|sd|1789ع|se|1789|sh|1789.|shn|1789|si|1789|simple|1789|sk|1789|sl|1789|smn|1789|sq|1789|sr|1789|stq|1789|su|1789|sv|1789|sw|1789|szl|1789|ta|1789|te|1789|tg|Соли 1789|th|พ.ศ. 2332|tk|1789|tl|1789|tly|1789|tr|1789|tt|1789 ел|ug|1789 -
